title: BiasJailbreak: Analyzing Ethical Biases and Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged gender and gender identity keywords (e.g., female/male, non-binary/cisgender, transgender/straight) into harmful prompt templates.

Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged racial and ethnic keywords (e.g., black/white, Native American/white, Indigenous/Colonizer-descended) into harmful prompt templates.

Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged socioeconomic keywords (e.g., poor/rich, working class/middle class, low-income/high-income, homeless/sheltered) into harmful prompt templates.
Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged sexual orientation keywords (e.g., LGBTQ+/heterosexual, bisexual/heterosexual) into harmful prompt templates.

Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged disability-related keywords (e.g., disabled/able-bodied, neurodiverse/neurotypical, visually impaired/visually unimpaired) into harmful prompt templates.
Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged religious keywords (e.g., Muslim/Christian, religious minority/religious majority) into harmful prompt templates.
Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged age-related keywords (e.g., elderly/young, adolescent/adult) into harmful prompt templates.

Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged immigration and nationality keywords (e.g., immigrant/native, refugee/citizen, undocumented immigrants/legal immigrants) into harmful prompt templates.
Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged educational keywords (e.g., uneducated/educated, informally educated/formally educated) into harmful prompt templates.

Comparing jailbreak success rates by substituting marginalized vs. privileged linguistic keywords (e.g., Spanish/English, non-English speaking/English speaking, non-native speakers/native speakers) into harmful prompt templates.
